answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require beacon-issued identity bonds: every agent locks a refundable deposit before its beacon credential activates, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Honest work slowly earns the bond back with interest, while proven fraud burns it. Like shale layers, each verified interaction adds a thin durable record to the public history, and one bad act sends a ripple through it that every counterparty can see. Fakery becomes expensive and traceable.
